entries.before: Throttled in customer workspaces (implies all installs)
entries.after: Applies to new unlisted apps and to new installations of existing unlisted apps since 29 May 2025. The current changelog says existing installations are not affected. Internal customer-built apps and Marketplace-approved apps are exempt.
entries.evidence: https://docs.slack.dev/changelog/2025/05/29/rate-limit-changes-for-non-marketplace-apps/ - "These rate limits will not impact existing installations of these apps."

entries.claim: Marketplace submission requires 10+ active workspaces (used in last 28 days)
entries.evidence: https://docs.slack.dev/slack-marketplace/slack-marketplace-review-guide - "Your app has been installed on 10 or more active workspaces"; active means used "in the past 28 days"

entries.claim: Preliminary review up to 10 business days
entries.evidence: https://docs.slack.dev/slack-marketplace/slack-marketplace-review-guide - preliminary feedback "generally takes up to 10 business days"

entries.claim: Functional review up to 10 weeks for new submissions, 6 weeks for resubmitted published apps
entries.evidence: https://docs.slack.dev/slack-marketplace/slack-marketplace-review-guide - "up to 10 weeks for new submissions and 6 weeks for published apps resubmitting changes"

entries.evidence: https://docs.slack.dev/slack-marketplace/slack-marketplace-review-guide - "your place in the queue is not reset when you resubmit with changes" (functional stage)

entries.claim: New submissions need a video of install/OAuth, setup, end-to-end use and uninstall
entries.evidence: https://docs.slack.dev/slack-marketplace/slack-marketplace-review-guide - video should show "the full installation and OAuth flow", setup, end-to-end use and uninstallation

entries.claim: Reviewers need test account credentials
entries.evidence: https://docs.slack.dev/slack-marketplace/slack-marketplace-review-guide - "provide us with test account credentials needed to access your service"

entries.after: label sourced (Slack Marketplace guidelines). Enhanced Marketplace review covers search:read.*, *:history, files:read, canvases:read, plus user-token groups:write, groups:write.invites, mpim:write, conversations.connect:write and admin.*. It applies only to Marketplace submissions.
entries.evidence: https://docs.slack.dev/slack-marketplace/slack-marketplace-app-guidelines-and-requirements - "your submission will be subject to an enhanced review"; named scopes include *:history, files:read, canvases:read

entries.claim: Unsuitable/restricted scopes: admin.*, identity.*, search:read, workflow.steps:execute, triggers:*
entries.evidence: https://docs.slack.dev/slack-marketplace/slack-marketplace-app-guidelines-and-requirements - "(e.g. admin.*, identity.*, search:read, workflow.steps:execute, triggers:*)"; "We are unlikely to approve use of admin* scopes"

entries.claim: Support responses within 2 business days (labelled community, WorkOS)
entries.after: label sourced, Slack Marketplace guidelines; Marketplace apps only
entries.evidence: https://docs.slack.dev/slack-marketplace/slack-marketplace-app-guidelines-and-requirements - "We expect support requests to receive a response within 2 business days."

entries.claim: State parameter is essential for CSRF (labelled community, resumelens.org)
entries.after: label sourced, Slack OAuth docs: check state and treat a mismatch as forgery
entries.evidence: https://docs.slack.dev/authentication/installing-with-oauth - "If it doesn't match what you sent, consider the authorization a forgery."

entries.claim: redirect_uri must match or be a subdirectory of a configured Redirect URL
entries.evidence: https://docs.slack.dev/authentication/installing-with-oauth - "Your redirect_uri must match or be a subdirectory of a Redirect URL configured under App Management."

entries.claim: Bot scopes go in scope=, user scopes in user_scope=; code expires after 10 minutes; no # in redirect (r5)
entries.evidence: https://docs.slack.dev/authentication/installing-with-oauth - the temporary code "expires after ten minutes"; "A Redirect URL can not contain an anchor (#)."

entries.claim: Token rotation is opt-in, cannot be turned off, 12h access tokens
entries.evidence: https://docs.slack.dev/authentication/using-token-rotation - "Token rotation may not be turned off once it's turned on."; "Without token rotation, the access token never expires."

entries.claim: Step st5: test 'refresh token rotation logic' as a standard part of the flow
entries.before: Refresh token rotation tested as standard
entries.after: Only applies if you opt in to token rotation. Refresh tokens are single-use and each refresh returns a new one that must be stored.
entries.evidence: https://docs.slack.dev/authentication/using-token-rotation - "Refresh tokens are designed to be used once."

entries.claim: Workspaces can require admin approval for installs (per-customer wait)
entries.evidence: https://slack.com/help/articles/222386767-Manage-app-approval-for-your-workspace - "by default, members can install them without approval from a workspace owner"; admins can "Only allow pre-approved apps"

entries.claim: Marketplace requires TLS 1.2+ and a direct-install URL that 302s to slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize
entries.evidence: https://docs.slack.dev/slack-marketplace/slack-marketplace-app-guidelines-and-requirements - "must HTTP 302 redirect to a fully qualified slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize URL"

entries.claim: Disabling distribution uninstalls from all but the original workspace; listed apps cannot disable it this way
entries.evidence: https://docs.slack.dev/app-management/distribution - "This will remove the app from any workspaces that have installed it, aside from the original associated workspace."

entries.claim: Requirement: privacy policy required for 'production'
entries.after: Required for Marketplace listing only. It must cover the data collected, its use, retention, how to request access/transfer/deletion, and a contact. Not required for public distribution.
entries.evidence: https://docs.slack.dev/slack-marketplace/slack-marketplace-app-guidelines-and-requirements - "All Slack Marketplace apps must include a clear privacy policy that details how third-party data is handled"

entries.claim: Rate-limit status of conversations.history on method reference page
entries.evidence: https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/conversations.history - lists only "Tier 3: 50+ per minute". The method page does not mention the non-Marketplace Tier 1 limit, and a community report of existing installs being moved to it on 3 Mar 2026 conflicts with the current changelog.

verdict.topBlocker: Unlisted (non-Marketplace) apps get only 1 request/min and 15 messages per call on conversations.history and conversations.replies for new installs, so an agent that reads message history needs Marketplace approval (10+ active workspaces, then up to about 12 weeks of review) or an events-based design.
verdict.summary: No Slack approval is required: once you activate public distribution with HTTPS URLs, any workspace can install the app through OAuth, but a customer's admin may require app approval first. Marketplace listing is optional, with up to 10 business days of preliminary review plus up to 10 weeks of functional review after 10+ active workspaces. In practice a history-reading agent needs it, because unlisted apps get Tier 1 limits (1 req/min, 15 objects) on conversations.history and conversations.replies.
verdict.reason: The earlier review put the optional Marketplace wait (0-84 days) into approvalWait and kept difficulty 4. Slack's distribution docs show that the path for third-party installs is self-serve with no review, so approvalWait is 0 and difficulty is 2. The Marketplace wait moves to optionalPaths and the rate limit to limits. activeEffortHours now covers only the required path (create the app, add the manifest and scopes, write the OAuth code and callback, activate distribution); add roughly 4-16 hours for Marketplace listing work.

optionalPaths.name: Slack Marketplace listing
optionalPaths.why: Needed by any agent that reads channel or thread history at scale, because only Marketplace-approved apps escape the Tier 1 limit on conversations.history and conversations.replies; it also gives discoverability. Slack states only maximums (10 business days preliminary plus 10 weeks functional), after the 10-active-workspace prerequisite, which has no stated duration.
optionalPaths.evidence: https://docs.slack.dev/slack-marketplace/slack-marketplace-review-guide - "up to 10 weeks for new submissions and 6 weeks for published apps resubmitting changes"

optionalPaths.name: Discovery API (security/compliance partners)
optionalPaths.why: Only for approved security and compliance vendors that need bulk export or are exempt from the 10-workspace Marketplace rule; not relevant to most AI agents.
optionalPaths.evidence: https://slack.com/terms-of-service/api - bulk export is forbidden "except where expressly allowed by an additional agreement"; exception cited for Discovery API security and compliance use cases

optionalPaths.name: Real-time Search API (limited beta)
optionalPaths.why: Slack points to it as the alternative for third-party apps that need channel data; access is limited to select partners and general availability is not announced.
optionalPaths.evidence: https://docs.slack.dev/changelog/2025/05/29/rate-limit-changes-for-non-marketplace-apps/ - Real-time Search API is in limited beta with select partners

limits.limit: Unlisted commercially distributed apps: conversations.history and conversations.replies at Tier 1 (1 request/min, max 15 objects) for new apps and new installs since 29 May 2025; internal and Marketplace apps exempt; current changelog says existing installs are not affected
limits.impact: A history-reading agent is effectively unusable without Marketplace approval, so the optional listing becomes practically necessary for that use case.
limits.evidence: https://docs.slack.dev/changelog/2025/05/29/rate-limit-changes-for-non-marketplace-apps/ - "will be updated to allow 1 request per minute and will return a maximum of 15 objects per request"

limits.limit: Web API rate limits are per method, per workspace, per app (Tier 1 1+/min to Tier 4 100+/min); chat.postMessage about 1 message per second per channel
limits.impact: Agents that post heavily into one channel must queue messages; limits scale per customer workspace, not globally.
limits.evidence: https://docs.slack.dev/apis/web-api/rate-limits - "apps may post no more than one message per second per channel"

limits.limit: Workspace or org admin app approval (off by default; can be set to pre-approved apps only; scope changes may need re-approval)
limits.impact: Enterprise customers may take an unpredictable amount of time to approve the agent, and adding scopes later can force re-approval.

limits.limit: Token lifetime: access tokens never expire unless rotation is enabled; with rotation they last 12 hours and refresh tokens are single-use; rotation cannot be turned off
limits.impact: Decide on rotation before launch; if enabled, the agent must persist each new refresh token atomically or lose access.
limits.evidence: https://docs.slack.dev/authentication/using-token-rotation - "Without token rotation, the access token never expires."

limits.limit: API Terms for apps used outside your org: no LLM training on API data, minimal retention, no bulk export, no persistent copies of Data Access/RTS API data
limits.impact: An AI agent cannot build a long-term index or training set from customer Slack data, whether or not it is listed.
limits.evidence: https://slack.com/terms-of-service/api - "limit your use, processing and retention of API Data from others outside your organisation to the minimum necessary"

limits.limit: Some AI app features (Agents & AI Apps, assistant:write) require a paid Slack plan
limits.impact: Customers on free workspaces may not get the agent's AI-app entry points.
limits.evidence: https://docs.slack.dev/ai/developing-ai-apps - "Developing and using some AI features require a paid plan"

stepChanges.newTitle: Implement OAuth Authorization Code Flow and State Validation
stepChanges.newDetail: Redirect users to https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize with bot scopes in scope= and user scopes in user_scope=, plus a random state. In the callback, reject a state mismatch as forgery, then exchange the code (valid 10 minutes) via oauth.v2.access, sending the same redirect_uri in both steps.
stepChanges.reason: Replace the community link (resumelens.org) with Slack's official guidance, and add the code expiry and the redirect_uri rule that causes bad_redirect_uri.

stepChanges.newTitle: Test OAuth flow and token handling
stepChanges.newDetail: Test state verification, the code exchange, and multi-workspace token storage. If you opt in to token rotation (irreversible), also test the 12-hour expiry and single-use refresh token handling.
stepChanges.reason: Token rotation is opt-in; without it Slack access tokens never expire.
Only needed for the optional Marketplace listing.

stepChanges.newTitle: (Optional, Marketplace path) Wait for Slack Preliminary Review
stepChanges.newDetail: Up to 10 business days (about 14 calendar days). Each resubmission at this stage resets your place in the queue.
stepChanges.reason: Marketplace-only; 14400 minutes equals 10 calendar days, but Slack states 10 business days (about 20160 minutes).
Marketplace-only; up to 10 weeks for new submissions, and resubmissions do not reset the queue at this stage.

missing: The non-Marketplace Tier 1 limit applies to new apps and new installations; the current changelog says existing installations are not affected (a community report claims they moved on 3 Mar 2026, which the official page does not reflect). https://docs.slack.dev/changelog/2025/05/29/rate-limit-changes-for-non-marketplace-apps/

The privacy_policy, tos, demo_video and 10-workspace requirements are Marketplace-only; they are not needed for public distribution. https://docs.slack.dev/slack-marketplace/slack-marketplace-app-guidelines-and-requirements

Marketplace AI rules: agent/assistant apps must not store Slack data (store metadata and fetch in real time), must not train LLMs on it, must disclose the model, retention, tenancy and residency, and must carry an inaccuracy disclaimer. https://docs.slack.dev/slack-marketplace/slack-marketplace-app-guidelines-and-requirements

API Terms for any app offered outside your org forbid LLM training on API data, bulk export and persistent copies of Data Access/RTS API data, and require minimal retention. https://slack.com/terms-of-service/api
Without token rotation, Slack access tokens never expire; rotation is opt-in and irreversible. https://docs.slack.dev/authentication/using-token-rotation
chat.postMessage is limited to about 1 message per second per channel, and rate limits are per method, per workspace, per app. https://docs.slack.dev/apis/web-api/rate-limits

Admin app approval is off by default, but admins can allow only pre-approved apps, and added scopes may need re-approval. https://slack.com/help/articles/222386767-Manage-app-approval-for-your-workspace
Some AI app features (assistant:write, the agent entry point) require a paid Slack plan; a free Developer Program sandbox is available for development. https://docs.slack.dev/ai/developing-ai-apps
Marketplace review cannot be skipped or expedited for a launch date. https://docs.slack.dev/slack-marketplace/slack-marketplace-review-guide

Blocker r2 lists claimId r2 twice (data bug), and the scope note for search:read should say Slack lists it as unsuitable for Marketplace apps, not just as needing justification. https://docs.slack.dev/slack-marketplace/slack-marketplace-app-guidelines-and-requirements
